Our own earlier verification file already recorded this reading (2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:720).

(2) CODE — confirmed, with one line of drift in the citation. `splitCommaSeparated` is `network-proxy-utils.ts:11-13` and is literally `str.split(',')`. `parseNoProxyRules` calls it at :222, not :221 (the page-relative anchor drifted by one; the identifier and behaviour are exactly as claimed), and its own docblock at :210 says `Parse a comma-separated NO_PROXY string`. No whitespace handling exists on any path; `normalizeProxyString` (storage.ts:2556-2559) only trims the outer edges of the whole string, and the Settings > Network field (AppSettingsPage.tsx:88) likewise only `.trim()`s.

(3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — the consequence is real, not absorbed by anything upstream, and the claim if anything UNDERSTATES the surface. Layer up: `pi-agent.ts:1466` spawns the Pi subprocess with `env: { ...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ... }`, so an operator who exports the documented space-separated `NO_PROXY` in their shell has it inherited straight into the interceptor when no in-app proxy setting overrides it (`proxy-env.ts:70-73` emits NO_PROXY only when `settings.enabled` AND `settings.noProxy` are set). `network-runtime.ts:197-215` restores the launch environment's NO_PROXY on disable precisely so an operator-provided proxy survives — i.e. the env spelling is a supported input, not an internal-only channel. Layer down: `getProxyForUrl` (interceptor :106-109) returns PROXY_URL whenever bypass fails and the wrapper sets it explicitly as Bun's `proxy:` fetch option (:2386, :2432-2434), which overrides whatever Bun would have decided from the env itself — so the mis-parse actively forces the request through the proxy. There is also a THIRD surface the finding does not name: `apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:216-218` builds Chromium's `proxyBypassRules` as `splitCommaSeparated(settings.noProxy).join(',')`, so every Electron session partition (browser pane, update feed, default) gets the same single bogus rule. No warning anywhere: the only proxy logging is booleans (`hasNoProxy: true`, network-proxy.ts:245-251) and a debug-only line (interceptor :112).

POSITIVE CONTROL (required for a silent-failure claim) — ran both parsers against the doc's own two example strings. Space form: one rule `{host: "localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"}`, and bypass=false for localhost:3000, example.com, api.example.com and 192.168.1.1. Comma form (the control on the same rig): four rules, bypass=true for all four URLs. The interceptor's replicated parser gives the same split (space -> false, comma -> true). So the failure is measured, not inferred.

correctedState: CONFIRMED, with the scope widened and one anchor corrected. Three surfaces split NO_PROXY on commas only, not two: (a) packages/shared/src/config/network-proxy-utils.ts:11-13 splitCommaSeparated, reached from parseNoProxyRules at :222 (the finding said :221) — this drives the Electron undici dispatcher and the headless server's fetch trust chain; (b) packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:84-86, the Pi subprocess, which reads the ENV spelling at :69; (c) apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:216-218, which pre-splits on commas before handing Chromium proxyBypassRules, so the Electron sessions (browser pane, update feed, default partition) lose the bypass too. Measured with a positive control: NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com" produces exactly one rule whose host is the entire string and bypasses nothing, while the comma twin bypasses all four hosts. The mis-parse is not merely inert — the interceptor sets Bun's explicit `proxy:` fetch option once bypass returns false (:2386, :2432-2434), so the request is actively routed through the proxy. Nothing warns: proxy logging is booleans only. The env spelling is genuinely reachable by an operator, since pi-agent.ts:1466 spreads process.env into the subprocess and proxy-env.ts only overwrites NO_PROXY when the in-app proxy is enabled with a noProxy value. Fix is one line — split on /[\s,]+/ in splitCommaSeparated's NO_PROXY caller and in the interceptor — but note splitCommaSeparated is SHARED with parseCertStoreSources (certStore, network-proxy-utils.ts:37), where the documented separator is comma only, so widen a NO_PROXY-specific splitter rather than the shared helper.
